prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [adversarial] Rowspan taller than its rows (language en).
Grid: 3 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Merged cells: "All three steps share on" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Step" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 2: header "Owner" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 48px
  col 3: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 76px · one-line width 1797px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Show the owner of each workflow step alongside a note shared by all three steps.","reading":"Readers scan the steps and owners row by row, then read the merged note as context for the whole sequence. The shared note can make the three-row group taller than the step and owner labels require.","groups":["Step and Owner form compact row-by-row pairs; Notes applies to all three pairs as a group."],"keep_intact":["Step names and owner names","Header labels","Unbreakable words in the shared note"],"may_wrap":["The shared note at word boundaries; its merged cell can use the height of all three rows."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [72, 85, 520] · table 678×146px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [62, 75, 582] · table 720×146px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r2A","good":"The step and owner labels are easy to scan as row pairs. The shared note fits in four lines without splitting words, and the table sits comfortably inside the viewport.","problems":"The Owner column has a little more space than its short labels need. The note’s last line is shorter than the lines above it, though the ragged edge remains reasonably balanced.","cause":"The 85px Owner width leaves 64px for text, more than the 48px needed for its header. The 520px Notes width determines the four-line wrap."},{"design":"r2B","good":"All labels remain intact, and the wider note is easy to read across the three-row group. The table uses the available viewport width.","problems":"The note ends with a particularly short fourth line, leaving a conspicuous blank area in the merged cell. The compact first two columns also feel less generous than in r2A.","cause":"The 582px Notes width changes the line breaks without reducing the note below four lines. The 62px Step width leaves only 41px for text."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"refine-r2A","widths":[72,80,520],"change":"Keep r2A’s comfortable Step and Notes widths while reclaiming 5px from Owner; its 59px text area still accommodates the 48px header."},{"name":"balanced-note","widths":[70,80,540],"change":"Give the shared note a modest increase in width to explore a different four-line wrap, while retaining comfortable space for the paired row labels."}]}
